_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the scoring weights: the top-level performanceComposite that blends the four supplier sub-scores, plus two risk composites (performanceRisk, which feeds the composite's risk_score component, and supplyRisk, the Kraljic Y-axis). Extracted from python/scores.py (composite + performanceRisk) and python/compute_analyses.py (supplyRisk) so every per-component weight is now an EXPLICIT normalized weight. For the risk composites each component's response curve is normalized to 0-100 in code and the WEIGHT here scales it; weight * 100 == the old point ceiling (country_distance 0.60->60, roster_concentration 0.40->40; supply_concentration 0.50->50, cost_premium 0.25->25, import_friction 0.25->25). performanceComposite is WEIGHTS ONLY: its components (quality_score/delivery_score/process_score/risk_score) are the EXISTING sub-scores computed by scores.py, not formula-defined, so they carry builtin:true and the future formula editor must never offer to edit their formula. Weights per composite MUST sum to 1.0. invertPolarity is a COMPUTE flag (=true applies the final 100-minus, performanceRisk higher=safer); performanceComposite uses invertPolarity=false because it is a weighted average of higher-is-better sub-scores (combine_score's clip is then a no-op). polarityLabel is the DISPLAY badge copy and is authoritative for the UI — never re-derive the badge from invertPolarity (they are different concerns: a compute flag vs display text). configuredIn links a built-in sub-score to the composite that PRODUCES it (risk_score -> performanceRisk); the two weight sets MULTIPLY, not add. ID CONVENTION (deliberate, not sloppiness): performanceComposite component ids ARE the scores.py column names (quality_score, delivery_score, process_score, risk_score) because these components are not formula-defined — they ARE those columns, and the id documenting exactly which column it reads is a feature, not a mapping layer that could drift. The risk composite ids (supply_concentration, cost_premium, ...) are unsuffixed because they are not columns. Consumed by python/risk_config.py (binding) and lib/risk-model.ts (types + loader). `version` is stamped into every printed report; bump it whenever a weight/enabled/polarity changes so a report remains reproducible from its stamp. Do NOT change weights without re-recording every affected baseline in the same change.

components.label: Quality
components.definition: Existing quality sub-score: per-PO defect rate + complaint rate, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Delivery
components.definition: Existing delivery sub-score: on-time-delivery % + average lead time, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Process
components.definition: Existing process sub-score: three-way-match pass rate, normalized 0-100. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Risk
components.definition: The performanceRisk composite output (structural: country distance + roster concentration, inverted so higher=safer). A built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Country distance
components.definition: Geographic supply-distance tier of the supplier's country. 0-100 lookup {Indonesia:0, ASEAN:30, Asia-Pacific:60, other:100}.

components.label: Roster concentration
components.definition: Roster-based supply concentration (the SAME curve as supplyRisk.supply_concentration), on the 0-100 axis {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Supply concentration
components.definition: Step curve on the number of OTHER suppliers in the same category across the full roster (active or not); fewer alternatives -> higher risk. Normalized curve {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Cost premium
components.definition: Spend-weighted item-price premium vs the cross-supplier benchmark, over supplier x item pairs with >=2 POs where the item has >=2 suppliers. Normalized clip(premium*250, 0, 100); at/below market -> 0.

components.label: Import friction
components.definition: Indonesia trade-agreement coverage of the supplier's country. Normalized {domestic:0, AFTA:32, RCEP-non-ASEAN:64, other:100}.
